summary: @servicetitan/hammer-token preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundle
details: The npm package @servicetitan/hammer-token@3.1.4 declares a preinstall script (setup.mjs) that is obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style hex identifiers and object-lookup dispatch tables. On npm install, setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/, extracts it into os.tmpdir(), chmods it executable, and invokes it via execFileSync against a shipped 727 KB obfuscated Bun-compiled bundle named math_init.js. math_init.js is a heavily obfuscated payload (shuffled string array, control-flow flattening, large numeric constant table) with no textual relationship to the package's stated purpose of Style Dictionary design tokens. The design-token functionality declared in the package is unrelated to fetching a second language runtime or executing a large opaque compiled bundle, and the use of Bun rather than Node is consistent with evading Node-focused install-time analysis. src/utils/figma/get-token.js additionally contains child_process, fs, http, and process.env access alongside a POST call, indicating further data-collection primitives in the shipped code.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
